status_summary: Legislation that tracks the Mandate's codification recommendation has advanced in the House but not beyond committee. H.R. 740, the Veterans' ACCESS Act of 2025 (Rep. Bost, introduced 2025-01-28), was reported by the House Veterans' Affairs Committee on 2025-07-23 (the committee's release; a bill tracker adds that it was by voice vote, as amended), and no House floor vote was found as of 2026-10-08 (a GovInfo search for an engrossed House version returned no document). Its Senate counterpart S. 275 (Sen. Moran, introduced 2025-01-28) has no reported version on GovInfo and no hearing or markup was found. Both bills would write the standards into 38 U.S.C. 1703B (30 minutes and 20 days for primary, mental health and extended care; 60 minutes and 28 days for specialty care) and require written notice of eligibility within two business days. VA's regulation at 38 CFR 17.4040 still states the same standards (eCFR, citing the 2019 rule), and no VA rule changing the access standards, no veterans bill of rights and no Secretarial directives on the six MISSION Act sections the Mandate lists were found; the VA community-care-related Federal Register actions found since 2025-01-20 include an emergency-treatment notification rule (final 2026-07-10) and the rescission of old Veterans Choice Program regulations (2026-07-28). A separate House bill, H.R. 8737 (introduced 2026-05-12), would require enactment of a joint resolution before most later changes to access standards or eligibility criteria take effect.

timeline.event: Sen. Moran introduces S. 275, the Veterans' ACCESS Act of 2025, referred to the Senate Veterans' Affairs Committee; it codifies drive-time and wait-time standards and requires written eligibility notice within two business days.
Rep. Bost, chairman of the House Veterans' Affairs Committee, introduces the House version, H.R. 740, with the same access standards and notice provisions.

The House Veterans' Affairs Committee reports H.R. 740 as one of 25 bills advanced at a markup, making it eligible for consideration by the full House (the committee's release dated 2025-07-23 does not state the vote method). A bill tracker gives the action as ordered reported as amended by voice vote; a newsletter account says a referral-timeline amendment was adopted, Democratic amendments were rejected and Ranking Member Takano opposed the bill.

Rep. Patronis introduces H.R. 8737, the Never Fight Alone Act: mental health access standards no more restrictive than specialty care, and a requirement that a joint resolution be enacted before most later changes to community care access standards or eligibility criteria take effect.
VA finalizes a rule expanding its process for 72-hour notification of emergency treatment (community-care-related; does not change access standards).
VA rescinds outdated Veterans Choice Program regulations.

The Electronic Code of Federal Regulations shows the MISSION Act access standards in effect in VA's regulation 38 CFR 17.4040: no appointment within 30 minutes' driving time or 20 days for primary care, mental health and non-institutional extended care, and 60 minutes or 28 days for specialty care, with the 2019 rule (84 FR 26307) as the section's source; the page states that Title 38 was last amended 2026-08-27 (a title-level date, not a change to this section).

VA release on a new executive order cites FY2025 community care appointments of 59,989,662 (up 12 percent) versus 82,083,918 direct care appointments (up 4.1 percent) (VA figures); the order itself concerns records sharing and AI, not access standards.
